# IATA.JK — house coverage rates it BUY (IDEATION re-stamp 2026-11-06)

Signal: coverage v3 carries a BUY with a Rp94 target against Rp72 (2026-11-04), +30.6% expected total return; base 95.8, bear 10.9 (−84.9%), bull 173.1. Why now: the primary leg is a DCF-to-end-of-life at Rp106.5 (70% weight, no terminal value) — the target is valuation-anchored, and the coal-life assumption is the one thing that can be checked against reserves.

**Regime: NEUTRAL.** Thermal coal is NEUTRAL at the desk: war premium still bids the energy complex, but the structural export-tailwind fade into 2027 is unchanged and named. That fade is precisely the bear case, so the stance carries no extra allowance — underwrite name-by-name.

Archetype: `commodity_capex_turnaround` (not `dividend_income_anchor`: the model expects **no dividend in the next 12 months**, so there is no yield to anchor on) · method card: VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL.

**Fast-disqualify checks.** (1) EV at the registry prior (0.42/+75/−35) = **+11.2%** — positive. (2) Target clears: DCF leg +48%, blended +33%, against a ~20%/yr annualised base-rate up-leg. (3) Sources: FY2026 reporting cited in the model [F54/F58/F65] and IDX filings, reachable.

**Questions for the deep-dive.** Cash USD1.45m against current liabilities USD77.35m — how is the wall refinanced, and at what dilution, before any coal price matters? Is the FY2026E 3.65 Mt volume anchor real, given it is derived from a 9M revenue figure divided by the model's own ASP? What happens to the life DCF if the export tailwind fades on the desk's 2027 schedule?
